what: Live check of the event worker (lab/functions/event-worker/index.ts) and the main service routes /_sb_events and /_sb_stats/<name> (lab/functions/main/index.ts, usage.ts) in ONE throwaway container launched by run.sh in this folder with the production launch flags (pinned image, 384m with swap equal, 0.5 CPU, 256 pids, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read only root, 32m noexec tmpfs for /tmp and the Deno cache, unprivileged user) and `--event-worker /home/deno/event`. Three functions were called (talk logs a line and an error line, burn runs a 40 million iteration loop, boom throws in its handler), the container was left for 100 seconds so the runtime drops the idle workers, and /_sb_stats/<name> was read with the service role token as the control plane does. Removed afterwards. Run twice: this record is the second run, after the event worker started signing with a key derived from the JWT secret, cutting batches by size and dropping a refused batch.

calls_and_probes.probe: forge events with the service role token
forge events with the anon token
forge events with a token of role sb_events signed with the raw JWT secret (what Auth could be made to mint)
read stats with the anon token

calls_and_probes.probe: the control plane's own token cannot post events

reading: The events arrive: each function has a bucket in the minute of its boot (boots 1 with its boot time, errors counted from the Error level log lines: 2 for talk, 1 for boom) and a bucket in the minute its worker was dropped (workers 1, cpuSum and memSum filled): burn used 59 ms of CPU against 10 and 12 ms for talk and boom, with about 10.5 MiB of memory at shutdown for each.
A function name that has not been seen answers known false with empty buckets and lines.

Nothing can post events but a token signed with the key derived from the environment's secret with role sb_events: the service role token, the anon token, no token, and a token of role sb_events signed with the raw JWT secret (what Auth, which signs with that secret, could be made to mint for a function that holds the service role key) are refused (401); the stats route refuses no token and the anon token (401). A bad name is 400.
The first events of the boot window (the worker boots before the main service listens) are retried by the event worker: boots were counted for all three functions.

Any function holding the service role key can read /_sb_stats/<name> for any function of its own environment (lines and numbers), as it can read the environment's data: the boundary is the environment.
not_established: a worker that is still serving after hours reports nothing until it is dropped (measured in the spike: Shutdown comes about 75 seconds after the last call)
